title: Channels
summary: Diceroll's Channels page in the Ship builds accent: only the channels that fit what Diceroll builds (iOS, Android, Windows x64, Linux x86_64), each in use with its delivery and sales state from one four-state vocabulary (Not set up, Ready, Live, Attention), the Not set up ones as cards that count only the person's steps and carry a Not using choice, One click when every credential is already held, a fit problem whose fix is the card's action, and the unavailable channels absent.
compare: The page, its Channels nav entries and every channel page are drawn in the Ship builds accent (release cyan), like Release tracks; green means Live, and Commerce only on Sales cards.

The header shows the product's platforms as chips with their CPU architecture where it matters (Windows x64, Linux x86_64) and their source ('from Diceroll's builds'); Publish 1.9.0 is the only filled button on the page, shown because 1.9.0 is not yet on every live channel. Turn on, Continue, Set up and Add an MSIX build are outline buttons.
The breadcrumb is 'Diceroll › Ship builds › Channels', the same path every channel page extends.

In use lists every Live, Ready or Attention channel, Polaris Key first: name, the version per track in words, what customers do, then Delivery and Sales as separate cells using exactly the words Live, Ready, Attention and Not set up, with an em dash for a channel that cannot sell.

Healthy states are status text: Live in green with a tick; Ready in default text with the info dot (never violet text that reads as a link), and Polaris Key's Sales Ready says why ('No offers yet'). Only Attention is a pill. Google Play's Attention row names the problem in one sentence (the key expires Oct 16, uploads and purchase checks stop then) with Replace key, and the same credential puts both sides in Attention.

What customers do is a quiet outline chip for every row (Obtainium included: 'Add to Obtainium · QR code'), lighter than the state cells. Long values truncate in the middle so the end survives ('play.google.c…com.example.diceroll', 'scoop install https://key.pl…scoop/stable.json'); Copy copies the whole value.

itch.io follows stable only (1.8.2 for Windows x64 and Linux x86_64, from the release workflow), so it never has a release before Publish. Platforms are written as people know them (Windows x64, Linux x86_64); butler channel ids appear only on the itch.io page's Setup tab.

Ready means set up and waiting for the next release (winget: the first winget-pkgs pull request opens when 1.9.0's stable rollout reaches 100%). 'Setting up' never appears as a fifth state: Steam is a Not set up card with its progress, and its sidebar entry shows '2 of 4'.

Not set up cards count only human steps and name what gets merged ('2 steps for you · submit to Flathub, then merge the pull request that adds the Flathub build'); Steam shows 'Step 2 of 4 for you' with Continue.

A fit problem makes the fix the card's action: Microsoft Store says it needs an installer (the build is a .zip; the Store takes .msix, .msi or .exe), offers Add an MSIX build (opens the docs on adding an installer to the build), and shows no Set up and no step count until a build fits.

One click appears only when every credential is already held (AltStore and SideStore: the GitHub App can write to example-org/diceroll); the card has the One click pill, no ring and no filled button, says there are no steps for you, and its outline Turn on opens one confirmation.

Every Not set up card, and every item once '3 more' is shown, has an overflow (⋯) whose item is 'Not using Diceroll on <channel>'; each channel page's header overflow has the same item. A recorded choice shows at the foot with who and when, and Undo ('Not using: Snap Store, chosen by Ana Lima on Sep 30').
No macOS, Mac App Store or Homebrew channel appears anywhere (page, nav entries, counts); the only trace is the scope line at the foot with Add it.
The remaining in-scope channels fold into one '3 more for your platforms' row with Show; no catalogue of every store is shown.

States to build that are not drawn: first run (only Polaris Key in use; the Not set up cards come first under one line saying what Polaris Key does for each); a row whose store can't be read keeps its last state words, dimmed, with one line ('Couldn't read Google Play at 09:12 · Retry'); loading draws skeleton rows in the same columns.

Sidebar (A-21): the Ship builds group is open with Releases, Release tracks, Rollouts, Channels (active, count 7), one entry per channel in use or being set up (Google Play with a warning dot, Steam with '2 of 4'), then Packages, Updates, Health. No Matrix, Outlets & feeds, Storefronts grid, Listing, App Store, Commerce or Outlet credentials item.

Words: 'channel' throughout, never 'outlet' or 'storefront feed'; a store's family is 'Store' (Steam, Flathub, the Microsoft Store), never 'App store'; store names exactly as the stores write them (App Store, Google Play, itch.io, winget).

Phone: the sidebar folds into the menu button, Publish takes a full-width row, the column headings go, each channel row stacks its name and meta with 'Delivery Live · Sales Ready' on one line under them (Attention there is warning status text with its icon), version and date tokens never break across lines, the customer hint hides, and the cards stack one per row.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: one filled button, the Ship builds accent everywhere, the Microsoft Store fix as the card's action, Not using reachable from every card, '2 of 4' instead of 'Setting up', and quieter, middle-truncated customer chips.

findings.issue: [visual] Two filled primaries: Publish 1.9.0 and the One click card's Turn on, which also had an accent ring.
findings.resolution: Turn on is an outline button; the card's ring is gone and the One click pill is the cue. Publish 1.9.0 is the only filled button.

findings.issue: [visual] The page accent (distribution green) collides with the success green and Commerce's colour, while the group label is release cyan and Release tracks used another accent.
findings.resolution: The console, the Channels nav entry and its channel entries are data-service="release" on all four console screens (Channels, App Store, Steam setup, Publish), so every Ship builds page is cyan. Green now means Live, and Commerce on the Sales card. areas.json still gives the area the distribution accent; that shared file is the lead's to change.

findings.issue: [flow] The Microsoft Store card shows a fit problem but offers an active Set up and a step count that leaves out the blocker; 'merge' is unnamed.
findings.resolution: The card's action is now an outline 'Add an MSIX build'; it shows no Set up and no step count until a build fits ('Set up opens when a Windows build is an installer'). Set up is omitted rather than drawn disabled, so the card has one action. Flathub names its merge ('the pull request that adds the Flathub build').

findings.issue: [flow] The foot records a Not using choice, but nothing on the page makes it.
findings.resolution: Every Not set up card has an overflow (⋯) labelled with 'Not using Diceroll on <channel>'; the compare adds the same item per expanded '3 more' entry and in each channel page's header overflow.

findings.issue: [copy] 'Setting up' in the sidebar and dialog reads as a fifth state.
findings.resolution: The sidebar shows '2 of 4' beside Steam (labelled 'Setup: step 2 of 4 for you') on all four console screens; the Publish dialog says 'Steam isn't set up yet (step 2 of 4 for you). Continue setup'.

findings.issue: [copy] Raw butler ids (windows-x64, linux-x86_64) instead of the header's names.
findings.resolution: The itch.io row says 'Windows x64 and Linux x86_64'; the ids are left to the itch.io page's Setup tab (compare).

findings.issue: [visual] Customer chips cut off the useful end, Obtainium has no chip, and filled mono chips outweigh the states.
findings.resolution: Chips are outline and muted; Google Play and Scoop truncate in the middle so the app id and manifest file survive; Obtainium has the same chip. Declined in part: Scoop is not shown as 'scoop install diceroll', because that command fails without a bucket; it keeps the real command, middle-truncated, and Copy copies all of it.

findings.issue: [phone] Version and date tokens break across lines, Google Play's pills wrap, the separator is missing.
findings.resolution: Versions and dates are no-wrap; the phone states line reads 'Delivery Live · Sales Ready' with the separator, and Attention is warning status text with its icon there, so every row's states fit on one line at 390.

findings.issue: [visual and states] Ready in --pk-info reads like a link; Sales Ready doesn't say what for; no first-run, loading or read-failure state.
findings.resolution: Ready is default text with the info dot; Polaris Key's Sales Ready adds 'No offers yet'. First run, a per-row read failure ('Couldn't read Google Play at 09:12 · Retry', state words kept) and a loading skeleton are compare items, as asked.
